Rashi on Chullin 70a:10:1.hebrew: אי נימא רובו ממש - ובבת אחת קא מיירי על כרחך, דאע"ג דשנינן לעיל "מחתך ומניח נעשה כו'", שינויא בעלמא שני אגב דוחקיה, ומתניתין במשמעותיה קיימא:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:10:1.english: If we say literally the majority of [it] - [meaning] that it is perforce speaking [of a case where it emerged] all at once; for even though we answered above, "[It refers to one who] cuts and leaves [each limb, so that it] becomes, etc.," [the Gemara] merely gave a forced answer because it was pressed, whereas the Mishnah stands in its plain meaning:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:11:1.hebrew: אלא לאו כגון שיצא חציו ברוב אבר - וקרי ליה רובו, דשדינן מיעוט אבר דגוואי בתר רוב אבר, והוה ליה רוב עובר:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:11:1.english: Rather, [is it] not where half of it emerged with the majority of a limb - and [the Mishnah] calls it "its majority," because we cast the minority of the limb that is inside [the womb] after the majority of the limb, and [thus] it is [considered] the majority of the fetus:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:12:1.hebrew: לא - לעולם לא הלכו ולא שדינן מיעוט אבר בתר רובא, ומתניתין ביצא רובו ממש. ודקשיא לך: "למאי איצטריך?" — כגון שהיה מיעוט אחד מן האברים משלים לרוב העובר, ואיצטריך לאשמעינן דהוי רובא, ולא אמרינן: "שדי מיעוט אבר שבחוץ אחר רוב שבפנים, וליכא לידה", אלא שדייה בתר רוב העובר, הואיל ובהדיה נפיק:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:12:1.english: No - In truth, they did not go [after the majority of the limb], nor do we cast the minority of a limb after [its] majority, and our Mishnah [refers to a case] where its actual majority emerged. And [as for] what was difficult for you, "Why was it necessary [to state this]?" — [it refers to] a case where the minority of one of the limbs completes the majority of the fetus, and it was necessary to teach us that this constitutes a majority [of the fetus], and we do not say, "Cast the minority of the limb that is outside after [its] majority that is inside, and [therefore] there is no [legally valid] birth"; rather, cast it after the majority of the fetus, since it emerged together with it:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:13:1.hebrew: כרכו בסיב - שגדל ונכרך סביב הדקל, כעין מרייל"א של גפנים:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:13:1.english: [If] one wrapped it in bast - [Bast is that] which grows and twines around the palm tree, like a tendril [Old French: merille] of grapevines:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:13:2.hebrew: מהו - שתהא חציצה, ואמרינן כיון דלא נגע ברחם לא קדיש, דהא רחם הוא דמקדש, דבדידיה תלא רחמנא; ולקמן בעי אימת כרכו. ואת"ל סיב הוי חציצה, דמין שלא במינו הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:13:2.english: What is [the law] - [Is it] that it is an interposition, and we say [that] since it did not touch the womb it is not consecrated, for it is the womb that consecrates, since the Merciful One made it dependent upon it? And later [the Gemara] asks when he wrapped it. And if you say [that] bast is an interposition because it is a different kind [from the fetus and womb, what is the law regarding his robe]?

Rashi on Chullin 70a:14:1.english: An afterbirth - does it constitute an interposition or not?

Rashi on Chullin 70a:15:1.hebrew: כרכה - אשה בידיה והוציאתו, והפסיקו ידיה בינו לבין הרחם; מי אמרינן: כיון דאורחיה הוא לילד את בהמתה, לאו חציצה היא:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:15:1.english: She wrapped it - [i.e.,] a woman [wrapped it] in her hands and brought it out, and her hands interposed between it and the womb; do we say [that] since it is the normal way to assist in delivering her animal, it is not [considered] an interposition?

Rashi on Chullin 70a:15:2.english: What are the circumstances - [with regard to] all these dilemmas:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:15:3.hebrew: אי דנפק דרך ראשו - ואחר שהוציאו אותו, עשו בו אחד מן הדברים הללו:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:15:3.english: If it emerged headfirst - and after they brought it [i.e., its head] out, they did one of these things to it:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:15:4.hebrew: פטרתיה - רישיה לרחם, וקדוש מיד, דהא יצא ראשו, הרי זה כילוד:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:15:4.english: Opened it - [meaning] its head [opened] the womb, and it is consecrated immediately, for [once] its head has emerged, it is [considered] as [one] born:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:15:5.english: [Where it emerged] feet first - and before the majority of it emerged, they wrapped it:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:16:1.english: A weasel swallowed it - inside the womb and brought it out:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:16:2.hebrew: הא אפיקתיה - כשהיה בלוע ולא נגע ברחם, והיינו "כרכתו":
Rashi on Chullin 70a:16:2.english: Why, it brought it out - [meaning] when it was swallowed and did not touch the womb, and this is [the same as the case of] "she wrapped it":

Rashi on Chullin 70a:16:3.english: Rather, [if] it swallowed it and brought it out, and brought it in and vomited it, and it emerged of its own accord, what is [the law] - does it become sanctified through this final emergence, or not:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:17:1.english: And entered [into] this [other womb], what is [the law] - Is the other animal exempted from [the law of] the firstborn, or not:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:18:1.hebrew: נפתחו - גרסינן. "נפתחו" — נתרחבו, שכשיצא הוולד לא נגע:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:18:1.english: They opened [nifteḥu] - This is the textual reading. "They opened" [means] they widened, such that when [the fetus] emerged, it did not touch [them]:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:19:1.hebrew: נעקרו - קס"ד קודם לכן נעקרו ונפלו:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:19:1.english: They were uprooted - [The Gemara] initially assumed [that] prior to this [the birth] they were uprooted and fell [out]:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:19:2.hebrew: הא ליתנהו - ומאן נקדיש? לא אויר ולא נגיעה, דהא אין כאן רחם:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:19:2.english: Behold, they are not [there] - And what would consecrate [it]? Neither airspace nor contact, for there is no womb here:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:19:3.hebrew: נעקרו - (קס"ד קודם לכן נעקרו) ונכנסו לפנים ונתלו לו בצוארו:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:19:3.english: They were uprooted - (it was initially thought [that] they were uprooted beforehand) and went inward and hung on its neck:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:1:1.hebrew: ואי אתמר בהא בהא קאמר רבה - מכאן ולהבא, דאי אמרת למפרע, קולא הוא דלא קדיש:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:1:1.english: And if it were stated in this [case, one might think that only] in this [case] did Rabba say - [that it is consecrated] from this point forward, because if you say [it is] retroactively, it is a leniency, as it is not consecrated:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:20:1.english: Were thinned - [Part] of the thickness of the walls was removed from the inside all around:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:20:2.hebrew: קנגעת בבעיא דאיבעיא לן - כבר, ומשם אתה למד את תשובתך:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:20:2.english: You have touched upon a dilemma that was raised before us - already, and from there you [can] learn your answer.

Rashi on Chullin 70a:20:3.hebrew: ויצא דרך פרוץ - מהו? מי אמרינן כיון דעומד מרובה עליו, הוה ליה כאילו כולו עומד? ל"א: נגממו מבפנים, ושפה חיצונה משמרת, וקא מיבעיא ליה תורא ברא מקדש או לא:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:20:3.english: And [the offspring] emerged through the breached [section] - What is [the law]? Do we say [that] since the standing [section] exceeds it, it is as if it were all standing [and the offspring is consecrated]? Another explanation: [The walls of the womb] were pared away from the inside, while the outer rim remains intact, and he is asking whether the outer wall consecrates [the offspring] or not:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:2:1.hebrew: מחתך ומניח - עד שיצא הרוב, ואע"ג שיצא הרוב והרי החתיכות לפנינו, משליכו לכלבים. אי אמרת בשלמא מכאן ולהבא הוא קדוש ומקמי יציאת רוב לא קדיש מידי — הנך דאיחתכו מקמי הכי לא חלה קדושה עלייהו; אלא אי אמרת דלמפרע הוא קדוש, הא כיון דרובא קמן, איגלאי מלתא ביציאת הרוב דמעיקרא קדוש להו:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:2:1.english: One cuts [each limb] and leaves [it] - until the majority [of the fetus] emerges; and even though the majority has emerged and the cut pieces are before us, he casts it to the dogs. It is well if you say that it is consecrated from [that point] onward, and prior to the emergence of the majority it is not consecrated at all — [then] those [limbs] that were cut off before then did not have sanctity take effect upon them. But if you say that it is consecrated retroactively, then once the majority is before us, it becomes revealed through the emergence of the majority that they were consecrated from the outset:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:3:1.hebrew: לא מחתך ומשליך - דכיון דליתנהו, אמאי תיחול בשעת גמר יציאת הרוב? ואיסורא ליכא, דהא כי שדא קמא חולין הוה. אבל ביצא שליש ומכרו לעובד כוכבים, וחזר ויצא שליש אחר, וכולן לפנינו — איכא למימר אגלאי מלתא וחיילא למפרע, ומבטלה מכירה:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:3:1.english: No, [we are dealing with] one who cuts and casts - For since they are no longer in existence, why should [sanctity] take effect at the completion of the emergence of the majority? And there is no prohibition [in his doing so], for when he cast the first [piece], it was non-sacred. However, where a third emerged and he sold it to a non-Jew, and then another third emerged, and all of them are before us — one can say that the matter is revealed [retroactively] and [sanctity] takes effect retroactively, and it nullifies the sale:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:4:1.english: Rather than teaching, "[If] a majority of it emerged" - which implies [that it emerged] all at once:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:5:1.english: [It] is regarded as though a majority of it emerged - all at once:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:6:1.hebrew: הלכו באברים - כדמפרש ואזיל, שיצא רובו במיעוט אבר — רוב העובר יצא, ומיעוט א' מן האברים השלים ליציאת הרוב. וקא מיבעיא ליה: הלכו באברים אחר הרוב, דנשדי מיעוט אבר שיצא בתר רובו שבפנים, והוי כמאן דלא נפק האי מיעוט, וליכא יציאת רוב עובר, ואם רצה מחתך ומשליך לכלבים. ומשום מטיל מום בקדשים ליכא, דמותר להטיל מום בבכור קודם שיצא לאויר העולם, כגון יציאת ראשו או יציאת רובו דרך מרגלותיו:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:6:1.english: Does [one] follow [the majority] with regard to limbs - As [the Gemara] proceeds to explain, [the case is] where its majority emerged through a minority of a limb — [meaning] the majority of the fetus emerged, and a minority of one of the limbs completed the emergence of the majority. And [Rava] raises the dilemma: Does [one] follow the majority with regard to limbs, such that we assign the minority of the limb that emerged to its majority that is [still] inside, and it is as if this minority had not emerged, so there is no emergence of the majority of the fetus, and if one wishes, he may cut [it] off and throw [it] to the dogs? And there is no [prohibition] on account of inflicting a blemish on consecrated [animals], because it is permitted to inflict a blemish on a firstborn before it emerges into the airspace of the world, such as [through] the emergence of its head or the emergence of its majority feet-first:

Rashi on Chullin 70a:6:2.hebrew: או לא הלכו - ושדינן ליה בתר רוב עובר, דלא שבקינן רוב עובר וניזיל בתר רוב אבר:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:6:2.english: Or [does] one not follow [the majority with regard to limbs] - and [instead] we assign it [the emerged minority of the limb] to follow the majority of the fetus, for we do not set aside the majority of the fetus and follow the majority of the limb.

Rashi on Chullin 70a:9:1.hebrew: אלא שיצא חציו - של עובר, ורוב אבר משלים אותו החצי, ואי שדינא למיעוטא דגוואי בתר רובא, נפק ליה רובא דולד:
Rashi on Chullin 70a:9:1.english: Rather, where half of it emerged - of the fetus, and the majority of a limb completes that half, and if I cast the minority [of the limb] that is inside after the majority, the majority of the fetus has emerged:

Tosafot on Chullin 70a:15:1.hebrew: כרכתו אחזתו - פי' בקונטרס: האשה כרכתו לעובר ואחזתו בידים, והפסיקו ידיה בינו לבין הרחם. וקשה לרבינו תם, דבשום מקום לא איירי באשה מילדת עם הבהמה, אלא רועה, כדתנן: "בהמה שמת עוברה בתוך מעיה והושיט הרועה את ידו". ורישא דהך מילתא נמי איירי ברועה: "כרכו בסיב" — לשון זכר; הכי נמי הוה ליה למנקט "כרכו ואחזו והוציאו"! ועוד, דמאי פריך "אי דנפק דרך רישיה פטרתיה"? וכי אין יכול להיות שאחזתו בידים בראשו ומפסיק בידיה בין ראשו לרחם? וזה דוחק לומר דאין לרחם לפתוח קודם שיצא הראש ואין יכול להכניס ידו. ועוד, דמתניתין ד"הושיט רועה את ידו" בלא הוציא כלל איירי, דאם לא כן נטמא במה שיצא; ואע"ג דיש לחלק בין מבכרת לאין מבכרת, אי נמי התם כשילדה אחר' קודם לזה שנפתח רחמה — כל זה דוחק. ונראה לר"ת כמו גרסת ר"ח: "כרכתו אחותו והוציאתו", שילדה נקבה עמו, כדאמר נמי בפ' כל הבשר (לקמן חולין דף קיד.): "אין לי אלא אחותו הקטנה, הגדולה מנין". ופריך: "אי דנפק דרך רישיה", וכן הנקבה, הא פטרתיה ראש הנקבה שיצא ראשה תחלה, שראש הזכר כרוך בין ברכיה. ומשני: דנפק מרגלותיו והוא כרוך בין ברכיה. וה"ה דהוה מצי למימר "כרכו אחיו", לענין איזה מהן בכור, אלא נקט אחותו משום דליכא בכורה כלל:
Tosafot on Chullin 70a:15:1.english: Wrapped it [and] held it - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: A woman wrapped the fetus and held it in [her] hands, and her hands interposed between it and the womb. And this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: for nowhere does [the Talmud] speak of a woman acting as midwife with an animal, rather [it speaks of] a shepherd, as we learned in the Mishnah: "An animal whose fetus died inside its innards, and the shepherd extended his hand." And the beginning of this very statement also speaks of a shepherd: "Wrapped it in bast" — [in the] masculine form; so too, [the Gemara] should have stated "wrapped it and held it and brought it out" [in the masculine]! Furthermore, what is [the Gemara] asking, "If it emerged headfirst, [the womb] has exempted it"? Could it not be that he held it in [his] hands by its head, interposing with his hands between its head and the womb? And it is forced to say that the womb does not open before the head emerges and he cannot insert his hand. Furthermore, the Mishnah of "the shepherd extended his hand" speaks of [a case] where he did not bring [it] out at all, for if not so, he would become impure through that which emerged; and even though one can distinguish between a first-birthing [animal] and one that is not first-birthing, or alternatively, there [in the Mishnah] it is when it gave birth to another [offspring] prior to this one so that its womb was already opened — all of this is forced. Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam like the reading of Rabbeinu Ḥananel: "Its sister wrapped it and brought it out" — meaning that it gave birth to a female together with it, as [the Gemara] also says in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaBasar (below, Chullin 114a): "I have only [derived] its younger sister; from where [do I derive] the older [sister]?" And [the Gemara] asks: "If it emerged headfirst" — and likewise [if] the female [did] — surely the head of the female has exempted it, as her head emerged first, since the head of the male is wrapped between her knees. And [the Gemara] answers: that it emerged hind legs first, while it was wrapped between her knees. And the same would apply that [the Gemara] could have said "its brother wrapped it," with respect to which of them is the firstborn; rather, it stated "its sister" because there is no firstborn status at all:

Tosafot on Chullin 70a:2:1.hebrew: מאי לאו מחתך ומניח ואי אמרת למפרע קדוש יקבר מבעי ליה - תימה, דלמ"ד נמי "מכאן ולהבא הוא קדוש", אמאי משליך לכלבים כיון דכבר יצא רובו? דהא ברוב מחותך נמי חשיב ליה לידה, כדאמר בהמפלת (נדה דף כח.): דיצא מחותך מרובו, אמו טמאה לידה. ומתניתין נמי קתני "ונפטרה מן הבכורה", ובכל ענין קאמר, בין שיצא אבר אבר, בין שיצא רובו בבת אחת. וי"ל, דבשלמא אי מכאן ולהבא הוא קדוש, כיון דאין קדושה חלה עליו עד יציאת רובו, א"כ מה שנחתך קודם יציאת רוב אין קדושה חלה עליו כלל, ויכול להשליכו לכלבים אף מאחר יציאת הרוב; ומיהו, מכי יצא רובו ואילך טעון קבורה למה שיצא, וכן משמע לשון הקונטרס. ואע"ג דקתני "יצא רובו הרי זה יקבר", ומשמע רובו בבת אחת כדמוכח בסוגיא, ומשמע אבל אבר אבר לא — היינו דוקא לענין המיעוט הראשון, דאפי' אותו מיעוט טעון קבורה כשיצא רובו מאחר דאין מחותך. אבל למ"ד למפרע קדוש, שמתחלה הקדושה חלה עליו מתחלת הלידה, א"כ במחותך נמי יקבר. ואמאי דמחתך נמי לא קשיא ליה היכי מטיל בו מום, דאיכא לאוקומי בנפל שאינו ראוי להקרבה, א"נ מחתך קודם שיצא לאויר העולם:
Tosafot on Chullin 70a:2:1.english: What, is it not [that] one cuts and leaves [it], and if you say [it is] consecrated retroactively, it should have said "must be buried"? - This is puzzling: even according to the one who says it is consecrated from now onward, why does he cast [it] to the dogs once its majority has already emerged? For a majority [that emerged] cut up is also considered a birth, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] HaMappelet (Niddah 28a): if it emerged cut up from its majority, its mother is impure [with the impurity of] childbirth. And our Mishnah also teaches, "and it is exempt from the law of the firstborn," and it states this in every case, whether it emerged limb by limb or whether its majority emerged all at once. And one can answer: Granted, if it is consecrated from now onward, since sanctity does not take effect upon it until the emergence of its majority, if so, whatever was cut off prior to the emergence of the majority has no sanctity taking effect upon it at all, and he may cast it to the dogs even after the emergence of the majority; however, from when its majority has emerged and onward, what emerges requires burial — and so implies the language of Rashi (haKuntres). And even though [the Mishnah] teaches, "if its majority emerged, it must be buried," which implies its majority [emerging] all at once, as is proven in the sugya — and implies, "but limb by limb, no" — that is specifically with regard to the first minority, for even that minority requires burial when its majority emerges, since it is not cut up. However, according to the one who says it is consecrated retroactively, where from the outset the sanctity takes effect upon it from the beginning of the birth, if so, even when cut up it should be buried. And as for the fact that he cuts it up, it is also not difficult for [the Gemara] how he may inflict a blemish upon it, because one can establish [the Mishnah] as referring to a non-viable fetus (nefel) that is not fit for sacrifice, or alternatively, he cuts [it] before it emerges into the airspace of the world:
